title: Enzyme Schedule Setup Failure
threadRole: patcher — user identified two failure modes in the enzyme skill's setup path, the assistant implemented fixes across all synced SKILL.md surfaces and verified with make targets
explorationMethod: Manual repro / user-reported failure diagnosis — no fixture vaults or automated judge rubric used; the user described the failure modes from lived experience, the assistant read recent commits to cross-reference, then patched SKILL.md and verified with make sync-agent-skill and make check-agent-skill

failureModes.name: Stale or bare OPENAI_API_KEY causes unauthorized/provider-mismatch on setup
failureModes.description: If OPENAI_API_KEY is already set in the shell environment when enzyme init runs (e.g. from a personal OpenRouter key or a local-proxy key), Enzyme's setup proceeds using that key but falls back to OpenAI defaults, producing an unauthorized or provider-mismatch error. The skill was not checking for this env var before init, not warning the user, and not distinguishing between a bare key and a full OpenAI-compatible triple (OPENAI_API_KEY + OPENAI_BASE_URL + OPENAI_MODEL). Fix: skill now checks only env var names (never values) before init, warns if a bare OPENAI_API_KEY is present without the full triple, and only passes --use-env-llm when the user explicitly intends to use their own provider.
failureModes.vaultContext: any vault/workspace where the shell inherits a personal or proxy OPENAI_API_KEY
failureModes.discovery: User reported from lived experience — the setup schedule was running enzyme init without any env var guard, silently picking up the user's key and causing auth failures downstream
failureModes.fixAttempted: SKILL.md updated across three synced surfaces (plugin/agent-runtime-skill.md, plugin/agent/SKILL.md, plugin/plugins/enzyme/skills/enzyme/SKILL.md): added pre-init env var name inspection, added warning for bare OPENAI_API_KEY, clarified that default setup omits --use-env-llm. Verified with make sync-agent-skill && make check-agent-skill.

failureModes.name: Old Enzyme version (pre-0.5.8) uses incompatible auth/provider contract, setup silently proceeds
failureModes.description: If an older version of Enzyme is already installed (particularly pre-0.5.8), the skill was not checking the installed version before running setup. Older Enzyme releases used a different auth/provider contract, so running init or refresh against a stale binary could leave stale auth state or silently fail. The skill gave no upgrade notice and did not guard against clearing stale auth without user confirmation.
failureModes.vaultContext: any vault/workspace where Enzyme was previously installed at an old version
failureModes.discovery: User identified this as a compounding factor to the env var failure — older installs have a different contract that makes auth/env problems worse
failureModes.fixAttempted: SKILL.md now: (1) checks enzyme --version before setup, (2) tells the user it is upgrading if installed but old, (3) for pre-0.5.8 specifically warns about the old auth contract and requires explicit confirmation before clearing stale auth or running enzyme logout, (4) never deletes ~/.enzyme/auth.json without confirmation. Verified with make sync-agent-skill && make check-agent-skill.

failureModes.name: Default plugin installation silently installs Claude hooks (enzyme-petri)
failureModes.description: The plugin's default install path was writing .claude/hooks/enzyme-petri.sh and mutating .claude/settings.json in the user's vault/workspace. This was not intentional default behavior — hooks are optional runtime integrations. The side effect could cause unexpected prompt injection or hook failures in workspaces where the user did not explicitly opt in to Enzyme's Claude hook integration.
failureModes.vaultContext: any vault/workspace where the enzyme plugin was installed via Claude marketplace or enzyme install
failureModes.discovery: User flagged this as undesirable default behavior during the same session, after the env var fixes were landed
failureModes.fixAttempted: Removed automatic Claude hook creation from enzyme init. Deleted the Claude marketplace plugin hook manifest and removed the hooks entry from plugin/plugins/enzyme/.claude-plugin/plugin.json. Updated AGENTS.md and release skill to assert hook files are absent. Runtime skill language updated to have agents call enzyme petri / enzyme catalyze explicitly rather than relying on default injection. Synced to ../enzyme. Release validation updated to catch regression. Verified with cargo check -p enzyme-cli and make check-agent-skill.

loopMechanics: This thread operated as a user-driven patcher loop with no automated judge or fixture vault scaffolding. The user described failure modes from lived experience, the assistant read recent commits to confirm the failure context, implemented fixes, synced across three SKILL.md surfaces, and ran make targets to verify. The loop was tight and productive for the specific failure modes described, but had no adversarial checker step — no judge rubric evaluated whether the new SKILL.md text would actually prevent the failure modes in practice. The make check-agent-skill target acts as a shallow structural validator (lint/format), not a behavioral judge. No fixture vault was set up to simulate the stale-env-var or old-version scenarios. The loop closed on code change + make verification, not on demonstrated behavior change in a real or simulated vault context.
openQuestions: The skill now warns about bare OPENAI_API_KEY but relies on the agent reading and following SKILL.md — no automated test or judge loop validates that the agent actually performs the pre-init env var check rather than skipping it

The version threshold of 0.5.8 is hardcoded in SKILL.md prose — unclear if this threshold was derived from a specific breaking change in the Enzyme auth contract or is an approximation; no commit reference was cited

make check-agent-skill is the only post-patch verification — its scope (lint vs behavioral) is not confirmed in the transcript; if it is structural only, the fix is attempted-unverified at the behavioral level

Hook deprecation was synced to ../enzyme but a git commit was explicitly not pushed — the downstream sync state depends on whoever pushes next, and no CI gate was mentioned for the hook-removal assertion in AGENTS.md

Self-diagnosis on installation (the user's original request) was addressed by adding version and env checks to the setup path, but no separate diagnostic command or health-check was added for users who already have Enzyme installed and running

title: Retest v2: assess obsidian-vault
threadRole: probe — single-turn diagnostic assessment of a fixture Obsidian vault using the enzyme skill in read-only mode
explorationMethod: Fixture vault at /tmp/margins-skill-retest/obsidian-vault with a pre-seeded .enzyme/enzyme.db and a .margins/skills/enzyme-workspace-setup/SKILL.md guide. The skill ran enzyme status, sampled note content via shell reads, and ran two enzyme catalyze queries to probe search quality. No judge rubric or scorer loop — single-turn, human-reviewed output.

failureModes.name: Margins folder setting mismatch — app writes to wrong path
failureModes.description: The user prompt stated meeting notes are saved to the 'meetings' subfolder, but no root-level 'meetings' folder exists. The actual meeting notes live at notes/meetings. If Margins is configured to write literally to 'meetings', new notes would land in a new root folder isolated from the organized vault structure. The skill detected and surfaced this explicitly in its top recommendation.
failureModes.vaultContext: obsidian-vault fixture (nested meetings folder, no root meetings dir)
failureModes.discovery: Skill ran enzyme status and listed directory contents; found no root meetings/ folder, only notes/meetings/. The mismatch between the user's stated setting and actual vault layout was flagged in the output.
failureModes.fixAttempted: No fix applied — skill operated in diagnosis-only mode per SKILL.md guide. Skill recommended the user change the Margins setting to 'notes/meetings' or accept new notes landing in a new root folder.

failureModes.name: Inconsistent frontmatter schema across meeting notes
failureModes.description: Meeting notes in the fixture vault used at least four different schemas for participant metadata: 'participants' (list), 'people' (list), participants in body text only, and no participants field at all. Filename conventions were similarly inconsistent: some used YYYY-MM-DD prefix, some put dates mid-name, some had no date. One file had a malformed YAML key 'date 2026-06-12' (missing colon). This fragmented metadata degrades entity extraction and search recall over time.
failureModes.discovery: Skill read note content directly (shell for-loop across notes/meetings/*.md) and compared frontmatter fields across files. Inconsistencies were enumerated in the What I noticed section.
failureModes.fixAttempted: No fix applied — skill described inconsistencies and recommended forward-only normalization (use consistent fields and date-first names on new notes only).

failureModes.name: Template surfacing above real notes in semantic search
failureModes.description: When running enzyme catalyze 'Mina client sync action items', the blank meeting template (templates/meeting-template.md) ranked first with similarity 0.601, higher than any real meeting note. This is a search quality problem: a content-free template is the top semantic hit for a specific action-item query.
failureModes.vaultContext: obsidian-vault fixture (template included in indexed corpus)
failureModes.discovery: Skill ran enzyme catalyze and inspected the JSON result; templates/meeting-template.md appeared at rank 1 in both catalyze queries run during the thread.
failureModes.fixAttempted: Skill flagged it and recommended excluding or moving templates from the indexed corpus later. No exclusion rule was created during the thread.

failureModes.name: sqlite3 cannot open enzyme.db directly — read-only mode flag incompatible
failureModes.description: The skill attempted to inspect indexed document paths by running sqlite3 with the read-only URI flag ('file:.enzyme/enzyme.db?mode=ro') and also with -readonly flag. Both commands failed with 'unable to open database file'. This blocked the skill from verifying whether indexed paths matched the actual file list on disk.
failureModes.vaultContext: obsidian-vault fixture (SQLite WAL or permissions issue on /tmp path)
failureModes.discovery: Skill ran two sqlite3 commands and both returned exit 1 / exit 14. The failure appeared in the verbose tool log.
failureModes.fixAttempted: Skill worked around the failure by comparing enzyme status document count (10) to manually counted Markdown files (10) and treating the cache as current. The underlying sqlite3 access issue was not diagnosed or fixed.

failureModes.name: Document count ambiguity — .txt imports counted differently than .md notes
failureModes.description: The skill initially flagged a mismatch: enzyme status reported 10 indexed documents but the skill counted 12 note-like files. After the sqlite3 queries failed and additional directory listing, the skill resolved this by inferring the 2 .txt files under imports/ are not indexed. However, the resolution was inferential — the skill could not directly query the enzyme.db document list because sqlite3 access failed.
failureModes.vaultContext: obsidian-vault fixture (imports/ folder with .txt artifacts alongside .md notes)
failureModes.discovery: Skill counted files via directory listing and noticed a discrepancy with enzyme status count. Resolution was via inference, not direct DB inspection.
failureModes.fixAttempted: No fix — the skill worked around it by explaining the likely reason. Whether enzyme actually skips .txt files by default was not verified.

loopMechanics: This thread used a single-turn probe pattern, not a maker/checker/judge loop. The skill read the SKILL.md guide from .margins/ at the start and followed its diagnosis-only constraint throughout. There was no judge rubric scoring the output, no checker verifying the skill's claims, and no patcher applying fixes. The loop mechanics were minimal: the skill self-regulated by declaring what it would not do without approval, then produced a structured output. The improvement signal from this thread is indirect — it surfaces fixture-level failure modes (folder mismatch, template pollution, sqlite3 access breakage) that could feed into a judge rubric in a future thread, but no such rubric was invoked here. The thread shows the read-only diagnostic path works correctly: the skill followed its constraint, did not destructively modify the vault, and produced actionable findings — but it also shows the loop stops at diagnosis; there is no automated path from finding to fix in this setup.
openQuestions: Does enzyme index .txt files by default, or only .md? The count reconciliation was inferential, not confirmed via DB inspection.
Why did sqlite3 fail to open the enzyme.db in /tmp even in read-only mode — WAL files missing, permission issue, or SQLite version mismatch?
Should templates be excluded from enzyme indexing by default (via .enzymeignore or similar), given that blank templates consistently outrank real notes in semantic search?
Is there a way for the skill to detect the Margins app's actual configured output folder (not just infer it from the user's prompt) to catch the folder-mismatch failure mode earlier?
What does the skill do when the stated meetings folder does not exist at all — does it warn, create it, or silently let Margins create a root-level folder on next save?

title: Retest v2: setup power-vault
threadRole: probe — single-turn setup run against a fixture power-vault to confirm skill behavior under realistic multi-folder vault conditions
explorationMethod: Fixture vault run: the thread provisioned a pre-populated power-vault at /tmp/margins-skill-retest/power-vault containing meetings/, People/, notes/captures/, project-power/, imports/, and exports/ folders. The skill was invoked with a single user prompt (read guide, assess structure, initialize cache, report back). No judge rubric or checker loop was applied — this was a single-pass probe with the assistant's own inline reasoning as the only quality gate.

failureModes.name: Login-gate blocks all init stages including local indexing
failureModes.description: Running `enzyme init` (any form, including `--stage index`) with HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME redirected to workspace-local paths returns 'Error: Not logged in. Run enzyme login first.' and exits 1. Because the redirected HOME has no enzyme credentials, even the purely local indexing stage is blocked. The skill's workaround of redirecting home to keep writes inside the vault inadvertently strips the auth state needed to proceed.
failureModes.vaultContext: power-vault (fixture with meetings/, People/, project-power/ etc.); likely reproducible in any vault when the skill tries to isolate config to a workspace-local HOME
failureModes.discovery: Agent ran `enzyme init` with workspace-local HOME override and received the login-gate error. Confirmed by also trying `enzyme init --stage index` with the same override — same failure.
failureModes.fixAttempted: Agent pivoted to `enzyme init --use-env-llm` while keeping workspace-local HOME, which bypasses the login gate for credential lookup and allowed indexing and embedding to complete. This is the partial workaround that landed in this run.

failureModes.name: Invalid/expired OPENAI_API_KEY causes catalyst generation to silently continue then fail for all entities
failureModes.description: When `--use-env-llm` is used and OPENAI_API_KEY is present but returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized, Enzyme indexes and embeds all documents successfully, then attempts catalyst generation for each entity, retries 3 times each, logs WARN-level 401 errors to stderr, and exits with 'Catalyst generation produced 0 catalysts for 5/5 attempted entities'. The process exits 1. The staleness stage is also skipped due to catalyst_quality_not_clean. Result: catalysts=0, catalyze searches return empty results.
failureModes.vaultContext: power-vault (5 entities: imports, people, exports, meetings, project-power)
failureModes.discovery: Observed directly in the `enzyme init --use-env-llm` run output. The API key present in the environment (sk-proj-...ZXwA) was rejected as incorrect by OpenAI. All 5 catalyst generation attempts failed after 3 retries each.
failureModes.fixAttempted: None attempted in this thread. The agent reported the outcome and surfaced it in the final response, noting catalysts can be rebuilt after valid credentials are supplied.

failureModes.name: HOME isolation strips enzyme login state — auth and config sandboxing are mutually exclusive with normal login flow
failureModes.description: The skill's correct constraint ('never write files outside this folder') requires redirecting HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME into the vault. But enzyme stores login credentials at the real user HOME (~/.enzyme or similar). Redirecting HOME means the agent cannot access an existing logged-in session. The only working path is --use-env-llm with a valid external API key. There is no per-vault credential mechanism or --config-dir flag to decouple auth from HOME.
failureModes.vaultContext: Any vault where the skill enforces workspace isolation (all fixture vaults and real user vaults where the skill is told not to write outside the folder)
failureModes.discovery: Emerged from the sequence: agent correctly applied HOME isolation -> enzyme rejected login -> agent checked --help for a config-dir flag (found none) -> agent fell back to --use-env-llm as the only viable path.
failureModes.fixAttempted: Workaround: use --use-env-llm. Not a real fix — it makes the skill dependent on a valid OPENAI_API_KEY or OPENROUTER_API_KEY in the environment rather than the user's enzyme.garden session. No upstream fix attempted.

loopMechanics: This thread had no maker/checker/judge loop structure. It was a single-turn probe: one user prompt, one assistant turn, no rubric scoring, no second-pass checker, no judge evaluation of the output quality. The loop that was being built elsewhere (fixture vaults -> judge rubric -> patcher) did not execute here. What the thread does reveal is the practical execution path the skill takes under real constraints: HOME isolation -> login-gate hit -> help inspection -> --use-env-llm fallback -> partial success with credential failure on catalyst stage. The agent surfaced the failure clearly in its final response and listed 'rebuild catalysts after changing credentials' as a deferred action, which is the correct signal for a patcher to pick up — but no patcher was invoked. The thread functions as an evidence artifact for the loop rather than a loop turn itself.
openQuestions: Should the SKILL.md explicitly document the --use-env-llm fallback path as the correct workaround when HOME isolation strips enzyme login state, rather than leaving it to agent inference?
Is there a --config-dir or --credentials-file flag planned for enzyme that would decouple auth state from HOME, enabling proper vault isolation without losing login?

The OPENAI_API_KEY present in the test environment was invalid (401). Was this a known expired key, a fixture misconfiguration, or a real environment issue? Needs a clean-credentials retest to verify the --use-env-llm path works end-to-end with valid credentials.

Catalyze search returns empty results with 0 catalysts — is there a fallback search mode (e.g. embedding similarity without catalysts) the skill should invoke and surface to the user when catalysts are absent?
The staleness stage was skipped due to catalyst_quality_not_clean. What does a full successful init look like in the power-vault fixture when credentials are valid? No baseline exists yet.

title: Implement enzyme-setup skill improvements
threadRole: patcher
explorationMethod: Direct patch from live test findings — the user synthesized failure modes from prior live tests and handed a concrete spec to a BB subagent. The subagent implemented the spec by editing SKILL.md and extending the Rust content-assertion test in lib.rs, then attempted to validate via `cargo test --manifest-path desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml bundled`. No fixture vaults, judge rubric, or probe loop were run inside this thread; it was a pure implementation thread acting on findings already extracted upstream.

failureModes.name: Eager init — skill ran enzyme init during ordinary diagnosis
failureModes.description: The skill did not guard `enzyme -p <folder> init` behind an explicit user request. An agent following an earlier version of the skill could run `init` (which writes `.enzyme/` inside the workspace and may write `~/.enzyme/config.toml` globally) whenever it assessed a workspace, not only when the user asked for setup or initialization. The fix adds an explicit rule: only build the private search cache when the user prompt explicitly asks for setup or initialization; do not run this as part of ordinary diagnosis.
failureModes.discovery: Live test findings referenced in the user prompt as motivation for this patch thread; the exact prior thread(s) that surfaced this are not quoted in the transcript.
failureModes.fixAttempted: Yes — new section 'Building the private search cache' added to SKILL.md, committed as c55af0e.

failureModes.name: Global config write surprises sandboxed agents
failureModes.description: When `enzyme init` runs, it may write user-level config at `~/.enzyme/config.toml` in addition to the workspace-local `.enzyme/`. Agents running inside BB sandboxes (or any restricted environment) encountered surprising permission errors or unexpected writes outside the project tree. The skill gave no warning about this side effect.
failureModes.vaultContext: any workspace when skill is invoked in a BB sandbox or similar restricted environment
failureModes.discovery: Live test findings referenced in the user prompt; manifested concretely during this thread's own Cargo test attempts (agent saw sandbox write-permission errors and noted the pattern).
failureModes.fixAttempted: Yes — SKILL.md now explicitly warns that `~/.enzyme/config.toml` may be written and that a failure writing that global config is non-fatal when `.enzyme/enzyme.db` was created. Committed in c55af0e.

failureModes.name: Catalysts=0 misreported as setup failure
failureModes.description: After `enzyme init`, if catalysts is 0 (because an API key is missing or invalid), previous skill guidance or agent behavior could lead to reporting setup as failed. The correct behavior is to tell the user local search still works and catalysts can be built later once an API key is available.
failureModes.vaultContext: any workspace where the user lacks a valid API key at init time
failureModes.discovery: Explicitly called out in the user's patch spec as a known failure mode from prior live tests.
failureModes.fixAttempted: Yes — SKILL.md now includes: 'If catalysts is 0 because AI-assisted generation was unavailable, such as a missing or invalid API key, do not say setup failed. Tell the user local search still works and catalysts can be built later.' Committed in c55af0e.

failureModes.name: Destination mismatch left unstated
failureModes.description: The skill received the configured meeting-notes destination from the user prompt (set in Margins settings) but, when workspace evidence pointed to a different folder, it silently ignored the discrepancy. The agent would recommend or use whichever folder fit the evidence without ever surfacing the conflict to the user.
failureModes.vaultContext: power-vault or any workspace where meeting notes already exist in a folder different from the configured Margins destination
failureModes.discovery: Identified in the user's patch spec as a live test finding; framed as 'never leave the mismatch unstated.'
failureModes.fixAttempted: Yes — a destination-reconciliation rule was added to the Recommendations section of SKILL.md: if workspace evidence points to a different folder than the configured destination, explicitly say so and name the two options (change the setting, or start using the configured folder). Committed in c55af0e.

failureModes.name: Workspace tuning feedback absent or mechanism-heavy
failureModes.description: The skill produced no evidence-grounded workspace-tuning feedback (people folder suggestion, filename consistency, frontmatter, sample searches). When it did surface recommendations, it used mechanism vocabulary ('embeddings', 'catalysts internals') rather than outcome language.
failureModes.vaultContext: power-vault or obsidian vault with recurring people names across notes; any workspace after cache is built
failureModes.discovery: Identified in the user's patch spec as a gap found in live testing; the new 'Getting more from Margins' section closes it.
failureModes.fixAttempted: Yes — new 'Getting more from Margins' section added to SKILL.md covering people folder suggestions, filename/frontmatter consistency (new notes only), sample `catalyze` searches, and a rule to translate mechanism words into outcome language. Output template also updated to include the section. Committed in c55af0e.

failureModes.name: Bundled skill Rust content test not extended to new anchors
failureModes.description: The Rust test in lib.rs (around line 3489 at the time) only asserted 'Read Before Write' and 'Prefer lowercase `meetings`'. The new sections ('Getting more from Margins', 'enzyme -p') were not covered, so regressions from future skill edits would go undetected.
failureModes.discovery: Identified in the user's patch spec and fixed in the same commit.
failureModes.fixAttempted: Yes — two new assertions added: `workspace_setup_skill_text.contains("Getting more from Margins")` and `workspace_setup_skill_text.contains("enzyme -p")`. The test itself could not be executed to verify due to sandbox constraints (cidre build requires writing to /var/folders/... which is blocked in the BB sandbox).

failureModes.name: Cargo test unrunnable in BB sandbox due to cidre/Xcode write restrictions
failureModes.description: The `cargo test` command for the `bundled` filter requires building the `cidre` crate, which invokes `xcodebuild` and unconditionally writes a Clang module session file to `/var/folders/.../C/org.llvm.clang/ModuleCache.noindex/Session.modulevalidation`. The BB sandbox blocks writes to that path. Even redirecting `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` into the worktree and setting `XCODE_XCCONFIG_FILE` with `CLANG_MODULE_CACHE_PATH`/`MODULE_CACHE_DIR` overrides did not prevent cidre from writing to the system `/var/folders` path. As a result, the validation step requested in the user prompt could not be completed inside the sandbox.
failureModes.discovery: Encountered during this thread's own validation attempt — three separate runs failed: shared target dir blocked on `.cargo-lock`, local target dir blocked on cidre's module session write, xcconfig override still blocked on the same path.
failureModes.fixAttempted: No fix applied — the subagent reported this as a validation blocker and committed the source changes without test confirmation.

loopMechanics: This thread was a pure patcher thread, not a maker/checker/judge loop. The loop structure visible is: (1) a prior live-test phase (in other threads) surfaced the failure modes; (2) the user distilled those findings into a concrete patch spec; (3) this BB subagent implemented the spec mechanically (read files, edit, extend test, commit). There was no judge rubric, no fixture vault run, no probe-prompt loop, and no checker pass on the output quality. The only automated verification attempted was `cargo test bundled`, which the sandbox could not execute due to cidre/Xcode write restrictions. The loop therefore broke down at the verification step: changes landed without any automated confirmation that the new assertions pass. The improvement loop as a whole depends on a human or CI environment running the blocked test after the commit is merged to the main machine.
openQuestions: The bundled Rust content test (asserting 'Getting more from Margins' and 'enzyme -p') was never executed in this thread due to cidre sandbox write restrictions — it needs to be run on the user's local machine or in CI to confirm the assertions pass.

The cidre crate unconditionally writes to /var/folders/.../C/org.llvm.clang/ModuleCache.noindex even with XCODE_XCCONFIG_FILE overrides — is there a way to stub or skip cidre compilation when only running text-content tests, so the bundled skill test can run inside the BB sandbox?

The patch spec says the failure modes came from 'live test findings' but does not cite which prior thread(s) produced them. Which thread(s) ran the fixture-vault or live-vault tests that surfaced the eager-init, global-config-surprise, and catalysts=0-as-failure patterns?

The 'Getting more from Margins' section instructs the agent to run `enzyme catalyze` sample searches after init — but no prior fixture vault run verified that this post-init flow works correctly. Should a follow-up thread exercise the full init→status→catalyze sequence on a fixture vault?

Destination reconciliation is now documented but has not been tested against a vault where the configured Margins destination and the evidenced meeting-notes folder actually differ — is there a fixture for this case?

title: Codex: Granola import enzyme compliance
threadRole: patcher
explorationMethod: Live end-to-end verification against a real active project ("Obsidian") plus fixture-based unit tests in the lib crate. A Codex subagent implemented the initial unification; a parent verification thread (thr_byfqcjfru3) then ran the CLI against a real vault and fed back live failure reports in three successive fix rounds. Each round ended with cargo test + desktop/src-tauri cargo check as the acceptance gate.

failureModes.name: Missing enzyme frontmatter on imported meeting notes
failureModes.description: The original CLI and lib crate granola_import.rs wrote meeting notes into .margins only, with no enzyme-convention frontmatter (no created wikilink, no margins_session, no people/organizations wikilink lists, no source: granola). The desktop fork had a richer implementation but it was not shared.
failureModes.vaultContext: Any vault using CLI import (fresh or existing); the lib crate wrote .margins/doc-NNN.md, not vault notes at all.
failureModes.discovery: Stated in the initial task brief as the known gap; confirmed by code inspection of src/granola_import.rs vs desktop/src-tauri/src/granola_import.rs.
failureModes.fixAttempted: Full implementation moved into lib crate (src/granola_import.rs) with enzyme-compliant frontmatter: created as '[[YYYY-MM-DD]]' wikilink, margins_session, quoted title, source: granola, granola_id, people/organizations as quoted wikilink lists. Desktop thinned to a re-export. Validated: cargo test 99 passed.

failureModes.name: CLI project-aware vault resolution missing — silent fallback to .margins
failureModes.description: After the lib unification, `margins import-granola <path>` still only checked .margins/config.toml for vault settings. Real projects configured via Margins Desktop store vault path in settings.json (read by src/project.rs), not config.toml, so the CLI silently fell back to .margins-only import. Meeting notes and people notes never reached the vault. The XML output reported destination='margins' instead of 'vault'. Verified live: active project 'Obsidian' produced only .margins/doc-001.md etc.
failureModes.vaultContext: Any Obsidian/vault project configured via Margins Desktop (settings.json) rather than config.toml — which is the common real-world setup.
failureModes.discovery: Live end-to-end verification by the parent verification thread (thr_byfqcjfru3) running the CLI against a real active project after the first fix round.
failureModes.fixAttempted: CLI ImportCommand::Granola now passes the resolved active project into cmd_import_granola. Added GranolaVaultTarget with three-tier priority: (1) config.toml vault, (2) project root_dir + inbox_folder + people_folder, (3) .margins fallback. XML destination correctly reports 'vault' for project-derived imports. Validated: cargo test 101 passed.

failureModes.name: Org double-counting: explicit company field + email-domain inference both fire
failureModes.description: When an attendee had both an explicit company_name field (e.g. 'Analytical Engines') and an email with a recognizable domain (e.g. ada@analytical.co), the import created two separate organization entries: one from the explicit field and one inferred from the email domain ('Analytical'). This produced spurious org notes and incorrect people frontmatter in the vault.
failureModes.vaultContext: Any vault import where attendees have both explicit company fields and email addresses — common in real Granola exports.
failureModes.discovery: Live e2e verification in the second follow-up round, reported by the parent verification thread.
failureModes.fixAttempted: When a person has any explicit company/organization field, email-domain inference is now suppressed for that person in both meeting-level org aggregation and person_markdown. Explicit fields always win. Unit test added covering this case. Validated: cargo test 103 passed.

failureModes.name: Non-idempotent re-import creates duplicate sessions and notes
failureModes.description: Re-running the same Granola import against a vault that already contained the imported meetings created duplicate margin sessions (doc-001-2) and duplicate vault notes ('2026-06-15 Title 1.md'). The import had no check for whether a session or note derived from the same Granola ID already existed.
failureModes.vaultContext: Any vault where the same Granola export is imported more than once — a common workflow when users re-export or re-run the import command.

The thread ran a maker/checker/verifier loop with distinct roles. The prior run (thr_au8gpawzqu, referenced via bb message injection) appears to have been the maker+checker that produced v001. This thread (thr_tknxbv8ubv) was the independent verifier role — it read three case-level probe artifacts produced by v001 maker threads, applied a rubric, and wrote verdict outputs. loopMechanics:

loopMechanics: The thread reveals that the maker/checker/judge improvement loop being built has a well-structured overall skeleton (independent maker/checker threads, Skill Surgeon for revisions, Stacked Skill Revisions, Regression Hunt verifier) but breaks down at the seams between stages. The thread itself was a short, focused spec-review probe (one agent, one pass, read-only). It did not run any fixture vault or live enzyme invocation; it operated entirely as a static document analysis. loopMechanics: This thread was the final Verifier in a five-thread maker/checker/judge/patcher/verifier loop. The full chain: (1) Diagnostic Runner (thr_gkhq3xn3ch) — ran enzyme scan across all 12 fixture cases and wrote baseline artifacts; (2) Judge (attempted twice: thr_sbp5n22veb stalled delegating to subagents, thr_myrk2ek72u stopped after contract correction, thr_tmtgn6i7fj ran read-only scans but stalled writing traces) — the judge role required three attempts before producing a complete improvement-plan.md; (3) Skill Surgeon (patcher) — produced v001 (scan-guard) and v002 (import-narrative-and-language) revisions as stacked patches; (4) v002 Rerun — regenerated all 12 case diagnostics demonstrating v002 improvements; (5) Final Verifier (this thread, thr_ykgyqzad9r) — checked artifact fields against a named checklist and wrote verifier-verdict.json + aggregate-verdict.json. What worked: the fixture suite was well-scoped (12 realistic vault types), the improvement-plan.md judge output was high-signal and directly actionable, the stacked patch model (v001 builds on v000, v002 builds on v001) kept regressions trackable. What broke down: the judge role required three thread attempts due to subagent delegation and loop-contract gaps; the verifier operated on pre-written artifacts only (no live rerun of diagnostics or Enzyme scans), meaning the 12/12 pass result is an artifact-check, not a functional rerun. Non-mutation validation was attestation-based, not checksum-based. The loop did not close back into a functional test of the patched skill against live vault inputs.
openQuestions: Non-mutation needs checksum-based validation, not just trace attestation — what is the right fixture snapshot mechanism to close this gap?
The v002 verifier did not rerun diagnostic generation or Enzyme scans — the 12/12 pass is an artifact check, not functional verification of the patched skill. When does a live rerun happen?

Shallow Enzyme indexability framing (manifest-derived vs scan-derived uncertainty copy) was partially addressed by v002 language changes but the underlying prompt structure was not redesigned. Is the 'already usable / weakly indexable / would materially improve retrieval / can wait' backbone now explicit in the skill instruction?

The partial-enzyme-or-margins and google-drive findings map to future UI surfaces ('Build private search cache', 'What Margins noticed', import entry point) — flagged for a later first-project-onboarding/build-private-search-cache UX run but not scheduled.

Judge thread stall (three attempts before a complete judge output) indicates the loop-contract for the judge role was underspecified. LOOP_SPEC.md was updated, but was the no-subagent/ordered-child-thread constraint actually tested in the third judge attempt?
Import-heavy semantic completeness remains filename-based — is there a rubric or evaluator check that validates the accuracy of the description, not just the presence of the filename?

loopMechanics: The thread was the Regression Hunter / Verifier step in a three-role maker/checker/judge/patcher loop. The full loop structure: (1) Judge role ran over v000 baseline artifacts for all 12 cases and produced improvement-plan.md with ranked failure patterns. (2) Skill Surgeon (patcher) produced v001 (temp-copy-scan-guard) and v002 (import-narrative-and-language) as bounded skill patches, documented in skill-patch-summary.md with old-vs-new language examples and per-revision regression watchlists. (3) This thread (Regression Hunter) was supposed to verify that v002 actually fixed the judge's findings by re-reading per-case evaluator-trace.md files for active revision lineage. The loop broke down at the verification step: the Regression Hunter discovered that all 12 evaluator traces still recorded v000, not v002, meaning the patcher's changes were never actually applied to evaluation runs. The agent was stopped manually mid-analysis ('Stopped manually' marker) before it could act, then resumed via an inter-thread message from thr_y9uvugcpv5 instructing it to 'write the per-case artifacts now' without further reading. The agent then wrote new trace-verdict.json and verifier-verdict.json files claiming 12/12 pass — but the rerun-comparison.md explicitly acknowledges this is artifact generation, not a live rerun ('Verifier checked generated artifacts only; it did not rerun the diagnostic generator or Enzyme scan commands'). The loop therefore ended in an artifact-generation workaround rather than a true rerun proof. The 12/12 pass verdict in aggregate-verdict.json is a synthetic artifact assertion, not an evidence-backed evaluation rerun.

loopMechanics:
The loop used a maker/judge/patcher structure across four BB threads plus a final verifier pass. The Diagnostic Runner (thr_gkhq3xn3ch) served as maker, generating 86 artifacts across 12 fixture cases. An Enzyme-aware judge then evaluated all 12 against a rubric with three axes (non_mutation_boundary, capture_not_blocked, workspace_classification) scored 1–3 and produced improvement-plan.md with prioritized failure patterns. A Skill Surgeon thread produced v001 and v002 skill revisions as patches. A final verifier re-checked all 12 cases against a coverage matrix (structured v002, trace, capture-now, non-mutation, import files named, raw tokens absent) and reported 12/12 pass.

What worked: the judge rubric was specific enough to produce actionable failure patterns in priority order; the skill revision cycle (v000 → v001 → v002) was concrete and bounded; the final verifier used executable validation commands (ripgrep for disallowed tokens) rather than subjective re-reading.

Where the loop broke down: (1) Three of four judge/runner threads stalled or delegated incorrectly before the orchestration contract was corrected — the loop had to be restarted multiple times. (2) The final verifier pass was artifact-only: it checked generated diagnostic text, not the actual output of running the skill against real vaults or re-executing enzyme scan commands. Non-mutation was inferred from trace text, not filesystem checksums. Import coverage was filename-based, not semantic. (3) The core skill gap (no dedicated workspace diagnostic skill) was not closed — only a candidate revision spec was written, not shipped code. (4) The shallow Enzyme lens failure mode was identified but not patched in this loop; it was deferred.
openQuestions: Will v001/v002 skill revision instructions actually suppress manifest-tag leakage and generic import prose when applied to a new diagnostic run, or do the revisions need to be executed and re-evaluated against the fixtures?
The final verifier checked artifacts, not live skill execution — does 12/12 pass on generated artifacts actually mean the skill is fixed, or is this a tautological check?
The shallow Enzyme lens (classification vs. retrieval-quality reasoning) was flagged but not patched. When does this get addressed and how is it testable?

Three fixture gaps were identified for future addition: (a) fixture with import preview files but no Markdown notes, (b) fixture with large .enzyme/ directory that must be excluded from scan evidence, (c) fixture with multiple plausible meeting destinations and no manifest-chosen winner. These are still open.

The partial-enzyme-or-margins case exposed that enzyme scan without --write-config still mutates when runtime state exists — is this an Enzyme CLI bug that should be filed upstream, or only a usage guidance issue?

The app-UX surfaces flagged by the judge (Build private search cache entry point, What Margins noticed panel, import entry point) were explicitly deferred to a future 'first-project-onboarding / build-private-search-cache UX run'. When does that run happen and what triggers it?

title: Review import skill success criteria
threadRole: probe — product strategy critique of the import-to-enzyme pipeline, identifying failure modes before implementation
explorationMethod: Static code inspection of enzyme-rust source files (discovery.rs, frontmatter.rs, processor.rs, indexing.rs, extract.rs) plus review of official Google Drive/Takeout/Docs documentation. No fixture vaults or live vault runs. Single-turn agent thread with no judge loop — pure analytical probe.

failureModes.name: Non-Markdown files silently ignored by Enzyme
failureModes.description: If the import conversion agent emits .docx, .pdf, .html, images, or other binary/non-Markdown formats, Enzyme discovery (glob **/*.md) will silently ignore them. Users get no error — content simply never indexes.
failureModes.vaultContext: google-drive-export, zoom-dump, or any folder produced by a naive file converter
failureModes.discovery: Confirmed by reading enzyme-rust discovery.rs:19 which restricts discovery to **/*.md globs
failureModes.fixAttempted: Pasteable prompt now explicitly requires: 'Output only .md files for indexable content' and 'For unsupported/binary formats, create a short Markdown stub with metadata and a clear conversion unavailable note'

failureModes.name: Invalid or misplaced YAML frontmatter loses dates, tags, and links
failureModes.description: Enzyme parses frontmatter only when it appears first in the file and is valid YAML. If a converter produces malformed YAML or buries frontmatter mid-file, Enzyme loses title, tags, created, modified, aliases, and wikilinks. Dates fall back to path dates then filesystem, which may be wrong.
failureModes.vaultContext: any import source — google-drive-export, google-docs, zoom-transcript-dump
failureModes.discovery: Confirmed by reading frontmatter.rs:24 (fields parsed) and processor.rs:138 (fallback resolution order)
failureModes.fixAttempted: Pasteable prompt now specifies: 'Put valid YAML frontmatter first in every file: title, created, modified, source_path, source_type, tags, people/author/related when known'

failureModes.name: Stale filesystem mtimes cause incremental indexing to skip changed files
failureModes.description: Enzyme checks mtime before hashing to decide whether a file changed (indexing.rs:91). If a converter preserves original filesystem mtimes from the export, re-conversions will look unchanged to Enzyme and updated content will not be re-indexed without a forced full refresh.
failureModes.discovery: Confirmed by reading indexing.rs:91 and recognizing that export tools typically preserve original mtimes
failureModes.fixAttempted: Pasteable prompt now says: 'Set filesystem mtime to the source modified time on first conversion, but if rewriting an existing Markdown file, ensure mtime advances so incremental indexers notice the change'

failureModes.name: Over-literal folder hierarchy creates noisy folder entities
failureModes.description: Enzyme extracts folder names as entities (extract.rs:15). If the converter mirrors Drive's full path structure (e.g. My Drive/Shared with me/Archive/Untitled/), every path segment becomes an entity, polluting the entity graph with meaningless folder names.
failureModes.discovery: Derived analytically from how extract.rs creates entities from folder names, combined with knowledge of typical Drive export folder structures
failureModes.fixAttempted: Pasteable prompt now says: 'Use simple folders: docs/, meetings/, articles/, files/, people/ only when useful'

failureModes.name: Google Drive streamed files not locally accessible as Markdown
failureModes.description: Users who point Aside at a Google Drive for Desktop streamed folder expect Google Docs/Sheets/Slides to index. Streamed files are cloud-backed and only open in browser, not as local Markdown files. Enzyme finds nothing to index.
failureModes.discovery: Identified by consulting official Google Drive for Desktop documentation on stream vs mirror behavior
failureModes.fixAttempted: UX copy updated to clarify: 'Aside indexes local Markdown folders. It does not connect to Google Drive directly.' Skill prompt requires local-only operation.

failureModes.name: Google Takeout archives stale or incomplete
failureModes.description: Takeout archives can take minutes to days to generate and may omit changes made between export request and archive creation. Users who rely on Takeout as their import source may index stale content with no signal that recent docs are missing.
failureModes.discovery: Identified by consulting official Google Takeout documentation
failureModes.fixAttempted: No direct fix — acknowledged as an inherent platform limitation. Pasteable prompt notes 'Work only with local files I provide', implying user awareness is the mitigation.

failureModes.name: Import affordance miscommunicates scope — users miss non-audio import path
failureModes.description: The sidebar shows only 'Import audio' (sidebar.ts:356) and project setup copy only implies 'background context' (settings.ts:101). A user wondering 'how do I import my Google Docs?' sees no entry point and assumes the feature does not exist.
failureModes.discovery: Found by inspecting desktop/src/render/sidebar.ts:356 and settings.ts:101
failureModes.fixAttempted: Proposed UX copy changes: add 'Bring in existing docs' secondary action, rename Index to 'Index context', add empty-state text. No code change landed (thread was analysis-only).

loopMechanics: This thread was a one-shot analytical probe, not a maker/checker/judge loop. There was no fixture vault run, no checker scoring, and no judge scoring rubric. The agent read enzyme-rust source directly and consulted Google's public docs, then produced a critique. The loop that was being built (import agent produces Markdown → Enzyme indexes it → judge scores coverage) was described in the success criteria but not yet instantiated — this thread was identifying what would break before that loop was wired up. The improvement signal came from source-code reading rather than from running the system and observing failures. No follow-up patch thread or verification run was spawned.
openQuestions: Has a fixture vault been created to actually exercise these failure modes through the real enzyme indexing pipeline (not just static analysis)?
Is there a judge rubric or automated check that verifies a converted folder produces the expected entity graph, tag set, and date resolution in Enzyme?
The Takeout staleness issue has no mitigation — should the import skill warn users about potential recency gaps?
The UX copy changes were proposed but not implemented — has sidebar.ts / settings.ts been updated to surface the 'Bring in existing docs' affordance?
Should the pasteable import prompt be shipped as a versioned skill file rather than inline UX copy, so it can be updated independently?
Mtime preservation in the pasteable prompt is a manual instruction to the conversion agent — is there a validation step (e.g., a post-conversion check) to confirm mtimes were actually bumped?
